ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The attached diagram shows a rectangular magnetic core with a coil wound on the left limb carrying current I. The right limb has a single narrow air gap labeled 0.2 cm. The diagram also shows 10 cm dimensions, consistent with a rectangular magnetic path; the problem text gives the mean core path length as 40 cm. Reasoning: The cross-sectional area is uniform and leakage/fringing are neglected, so the same flux density B is used in the core and air gap. For infinite core relative permeability, only the air-gap reluctance matters, so the applied ampere-turns are NI = B0*g/mu0, where B0 = 1 T and g = 0.2 cm. For finite relative permeability mu_r = 1000, the same ampere-turns must also supply mmf across both the air gap and the core: NI = B*(g + l_c/mu_r)/mu0. Equating the two expressions gives B = B0*g/(g + l_c/mu_r). Substituting g = 0.2 cm, l_c = 40 cm, mu_r = 1000: B = 1*0.2/(0.2 + 40/1000) = 0.2/(0.2 + 0.04) = 0.2/0.24 = 0.833333... T. Rounded to three decimal places, the flux density is 0.833 T.

Therefore B_2 = 1 * 0.2/(0.2 + 0.04) = 0.2/0.24 = 0.833333..., which rounds to three decimal places as 0.833 T.
